text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx and timeout rate in eu-west-2 for gateway cluster (5m avg 4.8%, threshold 0.8%). Paging oncall. See telemetry: https://telemetry.redwood.example/alert/1846789999

maya (oncall): Ack. I'm taking lead. Who's available to triage quickly?

kevin (pager): I'm on rotation. I'll start checking recent deploys and autoscaler events.

patrick (support): Customer channel shows several messages about intermittent timeouts starting ~2026-03-20T03:10Z. Two P2s opened (customer X & Y). No legal/legal-critical customers flagged.

olivia (platform): Noted. I see a small deploy of `gateway-proxy@2026-03-20T03:05Z` rolled out to eu-west-2 about 3 minutes before spike. Rolling back to previous revision could be fastest mitigation.

maya (oncall): Can we confirm error signatures? Are these 502/504/gateway errors or upstream 5xx?

tom (sre): Pulling upstream logs. Running `kubectl logs gateway-proxy --since=15m | grep -E "504|502|timeout|upstream"`

tom (sre): Logs show a mix: gateway 504 (upstream timeout) and 502 (bad gateway) with `connect ECONNRESET` to svc-search pods. svc-search health shows high restart_count on node ip-10-2-3-9.

kevin (pager): Node ip-10-2-3-9 shows oom_kill events at 03:07 and 03:09. That aligns with the deploy timing. Possible noisy neighbor or memory leak in svc-search after deploy.

olivia (platform): How fast do we want to rollback gateway? If svc-search is unhealthy, rolling back gateway won't help long-term but may reduce fanout concurrency and surface less downstream pressure.

maya (oncall): Immediate plan: 1) srem the problematic node from LB / cordon it 2) scale svc-search up by 40% to spread load 3) if not improved in 5m, rollback gateway deploy. Who can cordon node and scale?

kevin (pager): Cordoning node now: `kubectl cordon ip-10-2-3-9` and evicting pods.

kevin (pager): Node cordoned and evictions started.

olivia (platform): Scaling svc-search replicas from 10 -> 14 now (HPA takes a bit but manual scale applied).

tom (sre): After cordon and scale, 5xx dropped from 4.8% -> 1.6% in ~4m. Still above baseline but much better.

patrick (support): Updated customers: degraded for 20m, intermittent failures reduced. They're asking for specifics on what we did and next steps.

maya (oncall): Good. Keep customers updated. We'll keep monitoring for 15m. Sophia, can runtime check svc-search process memory patterns for the suspicious node?

(sophia (eng-runtime)): On it. Pulling heap and procmaps from the evicted pod on ip-10-2-3-9. Preliminary: native worker shows growing RSS over several minutes before OOM. Might be a regression in `search-worker v4.3.2` that's been rolled out yesterday.

olivia (platform): Can we isolate by routing a small fraction of traffic to pre-deploy version `v4.3.1` via gateway routing rules? That could confirm it's the new worker.

maya (oncall): Yes — set up a canary: route 5% to v4.3.1 for svc-search.

olivia (platform): Canary configured. Monitoring metrics for canary vs main.

tom (sre): Canary pods show stable memory and <0.1% errors; main pods (v4.3.2) still showing memory growth and occasional OOMs. Root cause likely in v4.3.2.

incident-bot: Incident severity adjusted P1 -> P2 after mitigation steps and customer impact reduction.

kevin (pager): Recommend we revert svc-search to v4.3.1 cluster-wide. That should be safe if canary is stable.

maya (oncall): Approve revert. Olivia, coordinate revert and post-revert monitoring.

olivia (platform): Reverting svc-search to v4.3.1 now via rollout undo. Rolling update begins.

olivia (platform): Rollout 60% complete. Error rate trending down.

tom (sre): After full revert, cluster 5xx returned to baseline ~0.2%. No more OOM events on that node.

patrick (support): Sent interim customer update with timeline, mitigations (cordon, scale, canary, revert), and ETA for postmortem. Customers asking for root cause analysis.

maya (oncall): Next steps: hotfix vs revert decision — we've reverted for stability. We need an action plan to find the root regression and prepare a patch. Sophia, can you reproduce memory growth locally or with stress harness on v4.3.2? Prioritize heap profiling.

(sophia (eng-runtime)): I'll run load tests with v4.3.2 and collect pprof/heap snapshots. If reproducible, we'll open PR with fix.

maya (oncall): Also: alerts and runbook updates. Current gaps: 1) node OOM alerting was not firing early enough 2) no automatic cordon on repeated kernel OOM events 3) no short-burst 5xx synthetic check. We need fixes. Assignments:
- tom: add alert `node_oom_events > 0` -> page infra team and oncall (due 6h).
- olivia: add automation to cordon node on >1 oom_kill in 2m (playbook + PR) (due 12h).
- kevin: update runbook 'service cascade' with cordon+scale+canary steps and example commands (due 4h).
- sophia: reproduce and attach artifacts (heap, pprof, flamegraphs) and propose code fix or revert guidance (due 24h).
- patrick: prepare customer postmortem draft and send to maya for review (due 8h).

tom (sre): I'll create alert PR and link to this thread.

olivia (platform): I'll start the automation PR for cordon. Will test in staging.

incident-bot: Created incident follow-up tasks in tracker: TASK-9821 (revert verification), TASK-9822 (alerts), TASK-9823 (runbook), TASK-9824 (customer comms).

maya (oncall): We're moving the incident to resolved for live impact. Keep thread open for action items and postmortem.

patrick (support): Customers acknowledged the interim update. No escalations.

kevin (pager): Leaving detailed notes in oncall log: commands used, node id, timing, and reasoning.

maya (oncall): Postmortem meeting scheduled: 2026-03-21 14:00 UTC in #postmortems. Please bring timelines and PR links.

sophia (eng-runtime): I'll attach heap dumps and test logs to the postmortem doc.

maya (oncall): Thanks team. Quick debrief: cordon+scale+canary+revert sequence is effective for model/service regressions that cause OOM cascades. We'll formalize in runbook.

incident-bot: Incident closed for live mitigation. Thread will be archived after postmortem doc is published.

maya (oncall): End of thread.
